blocks.text: Lazur is an AI assistant for illustrators on Mac. Hold ⌥ ⌘, ask out loud, and it answers while it looks at your screen. It can point at a tool, explain a setting, guide you one click at a time, and draft text. It does not draw, edit your files or click for you.

This page covers where an illustrator's computer day goes, what the research can and cannot tell you, and where a voice assistant fits. It also covers the client rules to check first. The small stops in the day are the part worth looking at first.
Where an illustrator's computer day goes

No one has published a time study for illustrators that we could open. We looked. Adobe's June 2026 report on creative professions covers wages, employment and BLS projections. It has no data on admin, email or software use. Treat any hour count for a typical illustrator with care, this page included.

The closest evidence comes from general knowledge work. Microsoft's 2023 Work Trend Index covered 31,000 full-time employed or self-employed workers in 31 markets. It found the average employee spends 57% of their time communicating and 43% creating. The report is from 2023, so that split may have shifted since.

The same report says 68% of people lack enough uninterrupted focus time during the workday. For an illustrator, focus time is the drawing. Every stop to find a menu or answer a client pulls from the same hours.

A 2023 survey of 251 US entrepreneurs found the average one spends 36% of the work week on small administrative tasks. The survey was commissioned by the author's own company, and it does not cover illustrators. Freelance illustrators run their own businesses, so the admin share may still feel familiar.
What to measure in your own week
Your own log beats any survey. Write down where your attention goes for one week. Use five labels only. App hunting means time spent looking for a menu, a setting or a shortcut you forgot.

items: Drawing: the strokes, the paint and the composition work.
Client messages: replies, revisions, file delivery and questions.
Admin: invoices, contracts, scheduling and bookkeeping.
App hunting: searching for a tool, a panel, an export setting or a shortcut.
Everything else: updates, file management, setup and small chores.

blocks.text: Log by the hour, not by the minute. Minute-by-minute logs are a chore to keep up. At the end of each day, fill in the hours while they are fresh. At the end of the week, total each label. The biggest label is the one to change first.

Here is a worked example. You draw in the morning, answer client mail at lunch, then lose a long stretch in the afternoon to an export setting you forgot. Under this method, that stretch goes under app hunting, not drawing. The fix is clear. You want faster answers for export settings, not a new drawing routine.
Why the time question matters more now

Figma's 2026 State of the Designer report, run with NewtonX on 906 digital designers, says 89% of designers feel they work faster. That is a self-reported feeling. The report gives no hours or task times, so treat it as a signal, not a measurement.

The US Bureau of Labor Statistics counts 51,900 jobs in 2025 for multimedia artists and animators, the closest category to illustrators. It projects 0% change from 2025 to 2035, which is 100 fewer jobs. BLS also says AI may dampen demand, because some animation and effects tasks can be finished faster with it.

Those numbers do not describe your week. They do show that time spent on tasks other than drawing is worth protecting. Faster answers on the repetitive parts leave more hours for the work clients pay for.
Where an AI assistant for illustrators helps, and where it stops

Lazur helps with the questions that break your flow. Where is this setting? Why did this change? What does this word mean in this menu? It answers those out loud, so your hands stay on the stylus or the mouse.

It does not replace the drawing. It does not decide your composition, fix a line or pick a palette for you. It is also not a plugin. It sees your screen and talks. When you ask how to do something, it guides you one click at a time and waits for each click.
Photoshop help for illustrators: the steps you ask about most

Hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask in plain words. Name the app and the goal. In Photoshop, I need more room above this title works better than help with canvas. Keep the menu or panel open on screen, because Lazur answers what it can see.

Canvas size is the common one. Image > Canvas Size opens the dialog, and ⌥ ⌘ C is the shortcut on Mac. Canvas Size adds or trims space around the art. It does not stretch your drawing. Image size is different. It resamples pixels, which can soften line art if you change it without care. Read the [canvas size guide for Photoshop on Mac](/how-to/change-canvas-size-in-photoshop) before you change either one.

Print work adds a question. Color mode decides how the file handles color. RGB suits screens, and CMYK is common for print. Ask your printer which one they want before you convert. Then ask Lazur to point at the Mode menu, so you convert from the right starting file. The [color mode guide](/how-to/change-the-color-mode-in-photoshop) covers both.
Figma steps for boards, frames and reusable parts

Press F for the Frame tool. In Figma, frames work like artboards for a client board or a set of thumbnails. Auto layout is ⇧ A on Mac. It spaces a row of items for you. Ask Lazur what changes when you add an item to an auto layout row, and it explains the spacing rule.

Components suit parts you reuse, such as a face, a prop or a logo lockup. Create component is ⌥ ⌘ K on Mac. When you edit the main component, its copies update. Name components clearly, so you can find them later in the Assets panel. Ask Lazur to point at that panel if you lose it.

Figma steps change between updates. When a menu moves, ask Lazur to point at the current one rather than trusting a guide written for an older version. Guides are a good start. The screen is the final check. The [frame guide](/how-to/create-a-frame-in-figma) and [component guide](/how-to/create-a-component-in-figma) cover the basics.
Client email, invoices and the admin around the art

Admin is where the day spills into the evening. It is also where dictation saves time. Hold fn to dictate clean text at your cursor in any app. Snippets handle the closing line you repeat on every invoice. A personal dictionary holds your studio name and your client names.

Apple's Mail User Guide for Mac covers searching for email and keyboard shortcuts. The guide is labeled for macOS 27. If you use Mail for client work, check the guide before you change a rule or filter. Lazur can explain a step while you keep the message open.

blocks.text: Always read a draft before it goes out. Check fees, usage rights and deadlines. A voice assistant can misread a number in a draft, just as a tired person can. You send the message, and you answer for it.
Client files, NDAs and what Lazur sees

Clients may limit who sees unreleased work. An NDA or a publishing contract can cover sketches, roughs and final art. It may also limit third-party software. Read your agreement before you hold ⌥ ⌘ over a confidential file.

Here is how Lazur handles what it sees. It listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored, and content is not used to train AI models. That describes the product policy. It is not a compliance certification.

If a contract bars outside AI tools, close the confidential file first. Keep a blank canvas or a menu open, then ask about the steps. You still get help with the interface, and the client work stays off the screen.
Mistakes people make with an AI assistant for illustrators

items: Asking for the whole job. Ask for the next step, then do it.
Holding the shortcut with a confidential file open. Close it first.
Trusting a menu path from memory. Apps move menus between updates, so ask Lazur to point at the current one.
Mixing up Canvas Size and Image Size. One adds space. The other changes pixel data.
Skipping the version check. Note your app version before you follow a guide. See [how to check your Photoshop version](/how-to/check-your-photoshop-version-in-photoshop).
Expecting Windows support. Lazur runs on Mac, on Apple silicon and Intel. Windows is planned, not available.
Sending a draft unread. Read it, edit it and send it yourself.

blocks.text: If you use Adobe Illustrator, check your system first

We could not confirm Illustrator's current version or its macOS minimum. Adobe's system requirements and release notes pages did not open for us. Check Adobe's own site before you update your Mac or the app. Once your versions are set, Lazur can point at the Illustrator control you need.
A realistic day with Lazur

The day plan above has eight moments. Most are a few seconds of talking. A few are longer, like a walkthrough or a research run. The point is to ask at the moment you get stuck, not after a long search.

Notice what is missing. Lazur does not draw the stroke, pick the color or send the invoice. You do those things. Lazur handles the questions between the strokes, plus the small admin that pulls you off the page.
Try it for a week on one app

Start with the app you open most. Ask a handful of questions a day for a week. Then read your log again. Did app hunting shrink? Did reply drafts take less time? Keep what helps and drop what does not.

Lazur has a free trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. Check the [pricing page](/pricing) for what each plan includes, and get the Mac app from the [download page](/download).
What Lazur is not

Lazur is not a plugin or add-in for Photoshop, Figma or any other app. It has no partnerships with any app maker. It sees the screen and answers. It does not click, edit files or run other apps for you.

Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. The run comes back with a summary and a report. Use it to find plugins, read tool docs or gather references for a client brief.
Next steps and related pages

If you work mainly in one app, start with its page. Photoshop users can read [Photoshop for illustrators on Mac](/for/illustrators/photoshop). Figma users can read [Figma for illustrators on Mac](/for/illustrators/figma). Designers who switch between apps can read [AI assistant for designers on Mac](/for/designers).

For single tasks, these guides go deeper: [how to add a new layer in Photoshop on Mac](/how-to/add-a-new-layer-in-photoshop) and [how to create a text style in Figma on Mac](/how-to/create-a-text-style-in-figma).

faq.question: Is Lazur an AI assistant for illustrators that works inside Photoshop?
faq.answer: Lazur is not a plugin, so nothing installs inside Photoshop. It runs on your Mac and sees the screen while you hold ⌥ ⌘. It points at tools, explains settings and guides you one click at a time in Photoshop, Figma, Canva or Chrome. It does not edit your file.

faq.question: Does Lazur draw or edit my artwork?
faq.answer: No. Lazur explains, points, guides, answers out loud and drafts text. You make every mark, color change and export yourself. It does not click buttons or operate apps for you.

faq.question: Does it work with Adobe Illustrator?
faq.answer: Lazur works with whatever app is on screen, but this page does not cover Illustrator-specific steps. We could not verify Illustrator's current version or macOS minimum from Adobe's own pages. Check Adobe's requirements before you install or update.

faq.question: Does Lazur store my client files or screenshots?
faq.answer: Lazur listens and looks at the screen only while you hold the shortcut. Audio and the screenshot go to AI providers to answer you. They are not stored, and content is not used to train AI models. Still check your client NDA before you share unreleased work.

faq.question: Can an AI assistant read my client email?
faq.answer: It can read what is on screen while you hold the shortcut. Use it to explain a message or draft a reply. Read every draft before you send it, especially fees, usage rights and deadlines.

faq.question: Does Lazur run on Windows?
faq.answer: Not yet. Lazur is a Mac app for Apple silicon and Intel Macs. Windows is planned, not available.

faq.question: How much does Lazur cost for an illustrator?
faq.answer: Lazur has a free trial with no credit card. The trial starts when you first open the app. Current plan prices are on the [pricing page](/pricing), so check there rather than relying on this page.

faq.question: What if Lazur gives me a wrong step?
faq.answer: Check the menu on screen first. Ask again with the app and the goal named, so Lazur can see the current state. Apps change menus between updates, so trust the screen over any guide, including Lazur's own answer.

faq.question: Is research the same as chatting with Lazur?
faq.answer: No. Research runs in Lazur's own Chrome tabs through the Lazur for Chrome extension. It comes back with a summary and a report. Use it for plugin lists, tool docs or reference gathering.
